judged_by: Carried over from qwen3-4b-harness-slots/coverage (Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-22; not yet checked by the labeler.) Claims the harness dropped are removed; repaired quotes were not judged for support.

question.note: Phrased as what the paper argues rather than asks, but the substance and quote are Q3's 'not only deprivation or personality, but also engagement'.

flags.text: Says engagement 'can lead to' more polarized and antagonistic behavior. The paper (abstract) says recent research suggests engagement 'may also be associated with' such behavior and disclaims causal claims.

question.note: Qualifying the classical view that engagement is benign is I2's content, in the wrong slot.

flags.text: Says hostile users 'have greater reach'. The paper says 'greater potential reach' and that this 'may' give them higher reach, not evidence of influence.

Says the paper argues against the idea that affective polarization is 'merely a correlate' of hostility. The paper argues against no such view; it says leader-directed affective polarization 'may be an antecedent, correlate, or consequence' of hostile interaction (p.14).

question.note: The conditioning role of affective polarization is T5, in the wrong slot.

central_claim.note: Lists interest, knowledge and online participation as examples, not as the strongest, so F1 is not credited here.

evidence.note: Accurate list of survey engagement measures (p.8); not a gold evidence item.

flags.text: Says the 9,250,180 posts were scraped 'from 2,567 panelists'. The paper gives 9,250,180 posts from its panelists and 2,567 linked panelists separately, with up to 3,643 respondents in X-only analyses; it gives no post count for the 2,567.

evidence.note: Names the SU word-embedding approach only.
Cosine similarity to the combined 'political hate' vector; per-user averaging not mentioned.
AFINN only; Perspective API not mentioned.
Accurate description of the leader thermometer measure (p.9); not framed as the L5 limitation.
RI-CLPM only; pooled OLS not mentioned.

key_findings.note: Gives the three indicators from the abstract but not that they are the strongest among several significant associations.

flags.text: States without qualification that more affectively polarized users show stronger associations. The paper says this holds for some indicators, clearest for participation, and is only partially consistent with Expectation 2 (p.14); the entry's own quote says 'for some indicators'.

key_findings.note: 'Beyond explanations based on deprivation or personality' is C2's 'not only deprivation or personality' (p.15, 'over and beyond personality' p.16); lacks the democratic-citizenship part.

scope_and_limits.note: Claim is L2, but its only quote is about network influence and does not support it. L2 is credited in the next two entries. Quote repaired by the harness; credit carried over from the claim.

flags.text: Says the paper does not demonstrate that the associations are due to time-varying confounding or reciprocal relationships. The paper's limit is the reverse: its RI-CLPM models cannot rule out time-varying confounding, measurement error or reciprocal relationships (p.10).

scope_and_limits.note: Big Five controls do not directly test personality accounts; does not say these are Dark Triad / sadism accounts or that those traits were not measured.

theoretical_positioning.note: Building on classical engagement theory is T1 (p.15). 'Extends' is T3 but the entry does not name the revisionist / dark-side view (its quote does); 'rather than just deprivation or personality' is the complementary stance of T4.

flags.text: Says the paper disputes a claim that hostile expression is limited to fringe audiences. The paper attributes no such claim to other scholars; the abstract only says hostile users 'do not simply cater to fringe audiences', and the literature it cites worries the reverse (discussions shaped by the most hostile voices, p.5).
